knowledgeBase.answer: My Wellness is your personal dashboard where you manage all your wellness journeys (care requests). You can see active and closed projects, view all practitioners you're connected with, track conversation status, leave reviews, and create new care requests whenever you need to connect with another practitioner.

A wellness journey is a care request for a specific wellness need. You create one by entering your wellness goal or symptom, selecting a category (Acupuncture, Nutrition, Yoga, Massage, etc.), describing what you're looking for, and specifying your location and travel preferences. Then the system finds matching practitioners for you.

Active care requests are wellness journeys you're currently working on or looking for practitioners for. Closed care requests are ones that have been completed (when you hired a practitioner) or canceled. You can see both on your My Wellness dashboard, organized in separate sections.

Once you create a wellness journey, click 'Find Practitioners' to browse matched practitioners for that specific project. The system shows you practitioners in your area with matching specialties, sorted by match quality. You can review their profiles and send connection requests.

When you find a practitioner you like, click 'Connect' to send them a connection request with an auto-generated introduction about your wellness need. They'll receive notification of your request. Once they accept, you can message them directly through your chat thread.

After sending a connection request, your match status shows 'Pending' while waiting for their response. They can either accept your request or decline it. Once they accept, your status changes to 'In-Progress' and you can start messaging them. If they decline, the status shows 'Declined' and you can search for other practitioners.

Once a practitioner accepts your connection request, a message thread opens where you can communicate back and forth. Messages appear in real-time, and you can discuss details about your wellness needs, scheduling, pricing, and next steps. All messages are saved in your thread history.

Messaging is disabled until the practitioner accepts your connection request. This is intentional—it gives practitioners control over unsolicited direct messages. Once they accept, full messaging is enabled and you can have a full conversation.

You can update a match's status using the dropdown in your message thread: 'In-Progress' means you're actively working with them, 'Hired' means you've decided to work with them, 'Not Hired' means you're declining to work with them. Once a match is Hired or Not Hired, it moves to your completed section.

When you mark a match as 'Hired', it means you've decided to work with that practitioner and the engagement is active. The match shows their name and a 'Hired' status badge. You can continue messaging them and leave a review once you've completed your work together.

After completing work with a practitioner (when the match is marked as Hired or Not Hired), you can leave a review. Click the 'Leave Review' or 'Update Review' button in your My Team section, add a star rating, and write your feedback about the experience. Reviews help other clients make informed decisions.

To close a wellness journey, click the × button on the project card or select 'Close Project' from the options. You can optionally provide a reason why it's closed (found another practitioner, no longer needed, etc.). Closed projects move to your 'Closed Care Requests' section and can't receive new matches.

When creating a wellness journey, you specify how urgent your need is. This helps practitioners understand your timeline. Options typically range from low (no rush, open timeline) to urgent (need help soon). Practitioners use this to determine if they can accommodate you.

When creating a wellness journey, you specify how you want to meet the practitioner: In-Person (at their office), Virtual (video/phone), or House Calls (they come to you). Practitioners filter by your preferences, so you only see matches who offer your preferred service type.

When creating a project, write a detailed description of your wellness need or symptoms. Be specific about what you're experiencing, any relevant history, and what you're hoping to achieve. This helps practitioners understand if they're a good fit and how they can best help you.

Your My Wellness dashboard shows two key stats: Total Care Requests (all your active and closed journeys), and Completed Care (the number of practitioners you've successfully hired and engaged with). These help you track your wellness activity over time.

The 'Open to Match' toggle controls whether your account is available to receive new practitioner matches. When enabled, your wellness journey appears in the practitioner matching system and they can see it as an opportunity. When disabled, your projects are hidden from practitioners.

When creating a wellness journey, you select from 8 wellness categories: Acupuncture, Nutrition, Yoga, Energy Healing, Herbal Medicine, Mental Wellness, Massage, and Naturopathic Medicine. Your selection helps the system match you with relevant practitioners.

When creating a project, enter your city, state, and zipcode. This information is used to find practitioners in your area (within reasonable distance based on travel preference). It's also visible to practitioners you connect with so they can confirm they can serve your location.

If you see 'No active wellness journeys' on your dashboard, you haven't created any projects yet. Click 'Create Wellness Journey' to get started. This opens a form where you describe what wellness support you're looking for and the system will find practitioners for you.

If a practitioner declines your connection request, their status shows 'Declined'. You can still search for other practitioners who might be a better fit for your wellness needs. Use the 'Find Practitioners' button to browse other options for that project.

Yes! You can create multiple wellness journeys simultaneously. For example, you might have one project for nutrition guidance and another for massage therapy. Each project is separate and can be at different stages with different practitioners.

The client inbox is where you view and manage all your match messages and conversations with practitioners. It displays all practitioners you've been matched with, shows message threads, and allows you to change the status of matches (Hired/Not Hired).

You can access your inbox from the main dashboard. The inbox displays all practitioners you're matched with in a threads list on the left side, and clicking any thread opens the full conversation and messaging interface on the right.

Match statuses in your inbox are: 'pending' (waiting for practitioner response), 'in-progress' (practitioner accepted and active), 'hired' (you selected this practitioner), or 'not-hired' (you declined this practitioner). The status dropdown shows available options based on the match state.

Click the status dropdown in the message thread and select 'Hired'. This marks the match as hired and automatically closes the associated project (changes project_status to 'hired' and sets closed_date). A confirmation modal shows the change.

When you change match status to 'Hired': (1) The match is marked as hired, (2) The project automatically closes and moves to 'Hired' status, (3) The hired_practitioner_serial is recorded on the project, (4) A closed_date is set, (5) All other matches on that project are also marked as 'hired', and (6) A status confirmation modal appears.

When you change match status to 'Not Hired': (1) The match is marked as 'not-hired', (2) The match closes but the project stays open (you can match with other practitioners), (3) The status is synced to the practitioner's side, and (4) A confirmation modal shows the status change.
No, hiring and not-hiring are terminal statuses. Once a match is marked 'hired' or 'not-hired', the status dropdown becomes disabled and you cannot change it further. The match is permanently closed.

The status dropdown is locked when: (1) match is still pending and practitioner hasn't responded yet, or (2) the match is already hired or not-hired (terminal status). It's only active once the practitioner accepts (in-progress status).

When a practitioner accepts: (1) The match status changes to 'in-progress', (2) The message input becomes enabled so you can message, (3) The status dropdown becomes available, (4) A notification is sent to you, and (5) You can now change the status to 'hired' or 'not-hired'.

When a practitioner declines: (1) The match status automatically changes to 'not-hired', (2) The messaging area shows a decline notice, (3) The message input is disabled, (4) You can no longer change the status, and (5) This match is closed and you can continue matching with other practitioners.

Open a thread by clicking a practitioner card in the threads list. Once the match is accepted, a message input field appears at the bottom of the thread. Type your message and click send. Messages only work once the practitioner has accepted the match.

If a match is still pending and the practitioner hasn't responded, the message input shows a 'Waiting for response' notice. Messaging is only enabled after the practitioner accepts (status becomes 'in-progress').

Click the 'Leave Review' button on a practitioner's thread card. A review modal opens where you can: (1) Enter a 1-5 star rating, (2) Write review text (5-2000 characters), (3) Upload up to 5 photos, and (4) Submit. The review is pending approval before becoming public.

If you already left a review, the button changes to 'Update Review'. Clicking it pre-fills the form with your existing review. You can edit the rating, text, and photos, then save the changes. Your updated review goes through approval again.

Reviews store: (1) Your rating (1-5 stars), (2) Review text (5-2000 chars), (3) Photos (up to 5), (4) Your name and client info, (5) Practitioner's name and serial, (6) Project serial, (7) Timestamp, (8) Approval status, and (9) Visibility status (public/hidden).
You can leave or update a review once a match is 'in-progress' (practitioner accepted). Reviews appear as a button on practitioner thread cards and also in the My Wellness dashboard on project cards.

Reviews are submitted with is_approved: false and is_visible: false. They're pending moderation by the admin. Once approved by admin, they become is_approved: true and is_visible: true, then show on the practitioner's public profile.

You can have multiple active matches (in-progress status) for the same project. Once you hire one practitioner, all other matches for that project are also marked as 'hired' and the project closes. You can also mark matches 'not-hired' to continue matching with others.

Yes. When you change a match to 'hired' or 'not-hired', the system broadcasts the status change in real-time to the practitioner's side. Their inbox automatically updates, showing the match as 'hired' or 'not-hired'.

The inbox has filter tabs: (1) 'All Matches' shows all active matches, (2) 'Messages' shows threads with conversations, (3) 'Closed' shows hired/not-hired matches that are complete. Each tab updates badge counts showing how many matches in that category.
Use the search field above the threads list. Search by practitioner name, project name, or service type. Results filter the threads list in real-time as you type.

Messages are preserved after hiring. The match becomes 'hired' and appears in the 'Closed' tab, but all previous messages remain visible. You can still view the conversation history with the hired practitioner.

Yes. You can match with and accept multiple practitioners for the same project. Each becomes an 'in-progress' match. You can then compare and eventually hire one (which closes the project) or mark others as 'not-hired' to keep matching.

The Inbox and My Wellness are two ways to manage matches: Inbox focuses on messaging and 1-to-1 match management (hire/not-hire status). My Wellness shows all projects and their match summaries. Both sync in real-time—changes in one appear in the other.

The inbox shows message delivery but not read receipts. You can see the conversation history and timestamps of messages. Real-time messaging updates the thread when new messages arrive from the practitioner.

supportResources.answer: Your client profile is a comprehensive wellness questionnaire that helps practitioners understand you better. It includes 10 questions about your wellness goals, health history, current challenges, lifestyle, preferences, and desired outcomes. This information is completely optional and helps practitioners personalize their care.

Your wellness profile is private and only visible to practitioners you have matched with AND who have already accepted your match. Practitioners cannot see your detailed profile information until they accept your connection request. Once accepted, they can view your complete wellness questionnaire.

The wellness questionnaire captures: main wellness goal, how long you've dealt with the issue, approaches that have resonated with you, allergies/sensitivities, current medications/supplements, typical day description, communication preference, biggest barriers to healing, prior practitioner experience, and desired success outcome.

You can edit your wellness profile anytime from your Client Profile page. All questionnaire responses can be updated, and changes are saved immediately. There's no limit to how many times you can edit or re-save your profile information.

The wellness questionnaire is entirely optional. You're not required to answer any questions. However, the more information you provide, the better practitioners can understand your needs and provide personalized care. Communication preference is the only field that has a suggested selection.

This question asks about your primary wellness objective right now. Examples include: better sleep, manage pain, reduce anxiety, improve digestion, increase energy, balance hormones, or address specific symptoms. This helps practitioners understand your main priority.

This question asks how long you've been dealing with your main wellness concern. Examples: 3 months, 2 years, since childhood. Knowing the timeline helps practitioners understand the depth and chronicity of your condition.

This asks about wellness approaches, modalities, or treatments that have been helpful to you in the past. Examples: acupuncture, meditation, herbal medicine, yoga, massage. This helps practitioners know what resonates with you and what to build on.

This question asks about any allergies, sensitivities, or medical conditions practitioners should be aware of. Examples: latex allergy, sensitive to strong oils, thyroid condition, pregnancy. This ensures practitioners can adapt their approach safely.

This asks about any medications or supplements you're currently taking. Practitioners need this information to understand potential interactions and ensure their recommendations are compatible with your current health regimen.

This question asks you to describe your typical day: work schedule, exercise, meals, stress levels, sleep pattern, hobbies. This helps practitioners understand your lifestyle context and how to provide recommendations that fit into your real life.

This asks how you prefer to communicate with practitioners: Email, Phone, Text/SMS, Video Call, or In-Person. Select the method that works best for you. Practitioners will try to honor your preference when following up about sessions or next steps.

This asks about potential challenges or obstacles that might make it difficult to move forward with your wellness journey. Examples: busy schedule, budget constraints, difficulty with consistency, skepticism about certain modalities. This helps practitioners understand and plan around your constraints.

This asks if you've previously worked with holistic practitioners or healers. Options: Yes, No, A Little. This helps practitioners know if they need to explain concepts or if you have existing experience with holistic approaches.

This asks you to paint a picture of what success would look like for you. Example: 'I have energy to play with my kids, sleep through the night, and manage my anxiety without medication.' This gives practitioners a clear vision of your ideal outcome.

Your basic profile includes: Age, Sex, City/State/Zipcode. This information helps practitioners understand your geographic location and some demographic context. This basic info is visible to practitioners who have accepted your match.

Your profile is viewable at your client public profile page. Practitioners who have accepted your match can visit this page which displays your basic information, wellness goal, health history, allergies, medications, daily routine, preferences, and any barriers to healing.

Important: Your wellness profile information is NOT used for practitioner matching. Matches are based solely on your project category, subcategory, location, and availability. Your profile is provided to practitioners after matching to help them understand you better and personalize their care.

You can leave the wellness questionnaire incomplete and save your progress. No fields are required, so you can add information gradually as you're comfortable. You can always return to your profile page and add more details later.

Your profile information is only shared with practitioners you've explicitly matched with AND who have accepted your match. It's never shown to practitioners during the initial matching process, only after they accept your connection request. Your privacy is protected at all stages.

Your Settings page is where you manage your account, notification preferences, memberships, and security. You can access it from your dashboard. The settings are organized into tabs: Account, Notifications, Memberships, and Security.

To change your email, go to Settings > Account and click Edit next to your email address. Enter your new email and submit. A confirmation link will be sent to your new email. Click the link to verify and complete the change.

To change your password, go to Settings > Security and click 'Change Password'. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Click the link in the email to set a new password. You must confirm before the change takes effect.

Go to Settings > Notifications to manage how you receive notifications. You can control notifications for: Practitioner Messages, Matches, Promotions, and Account & Security alerts. For each, choose to receive In-App, Email, or SMS notifications.

Practitioner Message notifications alert you when a practitioner messages you or accepts your match request. You can receive these via: In-App (notification bell), Email (to your email address), or SMS (text message).

Match notifications alert you when a practitioner accepts or declines your connection request. You can receive these via: In-App (notification bell), Email (to your email address), or SMS (text message).

Promotion notifications are special offers and updates from Rooted Vitality. You can enable/disable these in Settings > Notifications under 'Promotions'. When enabled, you'll receive offers about new features or services.

Account & Security notifications are critical alerts about your account, such as password changes, email updates, or suspicious login attempts. These are important for your security and are recommended to stay enabled.

There are 3 notification channels: In-App (appears in your notification bell), Email (sent to your email address), SMS (sent as text message). For each notification type, you can choose which channels to use.
Notification preferences are saved automatically when you check or uncheck a box. You'll see a confirmation message that preferences were updated. Changes take effect immediately.

By default, all notification channels are enabled when you sign up. This means you'll receive in-app, email, and SMS notifications for all notification types (messages, matches, promotions, account alerts).

To disable a notification type, go to Settings > Notifications and uncheck the boxes for the channels you don't want. For example, uncheck 'Email' to stop receiving emails but still get in-app notifications.
Email and SMS notifications are sent to the contact information in your Account Settings (Settings > Account). This is the primary email address associated with your Rooted Vitality account.

The Memberships section in Settings shows your current subscription status with Rooted Vitality. It displays your membership type, renewal date, and any benefits. Client memberships are typically included with your account.
The Security section in Settings manages your account security. This includes password management, and security alerts. This section helps protect your account from unauthorized access.

To edit account information, go to Settings > Account. Click the Edit button next to the field you want to change (email, password, etc.). Make your changes and save. Your updates are synced to the database immediately.
Your Account section displays: Email Address, Password (shown as dots for security), Age, Sex, and Location. Some fields are editable (click Edit), while others are read-only display fields.

Notifications appear in your notification bell in the header. In-app notifications are typically kept for a session. For a record of important notifications (like match updates), check your email inbox for email notifications.

There's no 'reset all' option in Settings. To return to default notification preferences, go to Settings > Notifications and manually check all boxes for the channels you want. This restores them to the default 'all enabled' state.
